negatives.observed: An independent staged-name hash check attempted to use Convert.ToHexString, but the available Windows PowerShell/.NET surface did not provide that method, so the command returned a null hash.
negatives.recovery: Retain the failed check, compute the SHA-256 with the portable BitConverter byte-to-hex path, and compare it with the frozen staged-name receipt.

negatives.observed: A combined evidence-script inspection returned exit code one because an optional ripgrep term had no match, even though the requested source excerpt was read successfully.
negatives.recovery: Retain the wrapper failure, separate required reads from optional searches, and treat a bounded no-match search as an inspected absence rather than allowing it to mask successful output.

negatives.observed: A broad recursive search for privacy and raw-ID scanner names exceeded its bounded command timeout without returning a tool path.
negatives.recovery: Retain the timeout, narrow discovery to known phase tooling and direct script-directory metadata, then run the located scanner with an explicit bounded scope.

boundary: Operational failures are retained as execution evidence and do not close any external gate.
